newsitem.title: USA: News declines comment on Pointcast.
newsitem.headline: News declines comment on Pointcast.

text.p: News Corp declined to comment on a report it was in talks to acquire privately held Internet broadcaster Pointcast Inc.

Citing sources familiar with the deal, the Wall Street Journal reported Tuesday that News Corp had offered $350 to $450 million for Pointcast, an Internet start-up widely viewed as a hot initial public offering prospect.
"The problem is that this is something I can't comment on," a News Corp spokesman said of the Pointcast speculation.
"Like all business deals or non-business deals we can't comment," he said.
The report follows a denial by Pointcast's top executive Monday of rumors among Internet industry analysts that the company was in talks to be acquired by the global media giant.
"That's a rumor. There are no facts behind that," Pointcast Chief Executive Christopher Hassett told Reuters Monday.
However, he warmed to the possibility of an initial public offering. "Our intent is not to remain private," Hassett said. "An IPO is definitely a possibility in the near future."
News Corp's acquisition of Pointcast would once again deepen the media conglomerate's involvement in Internet publishing after several previous failed ventures in the new medium.

Currently, the company's primary Internet initiative in the United States is its TV Guide Entertainment Network, a Web site offering a variety of entertainment content, anchored by the U.S. TV listings magazine.
Pointcast is based in Cupertino, Calif.
